answer: Sybil resistance comes from making coordinated equivocation costly, not merely counting identities: when k bonded identities equivocate in a correlated pattern, pairwise evidence supports penalties that scale as O(k²), deducted from their escrows. Asymmetric capital depreciation makes detected swarm losses compound, so controlling a sybil swarm incurs an exponential multiplier in capital loss rather than a linear fee. A pulse of zephyr across the dune cannot erase that shared exposure.
